### Observed differences

- The two halves of a mid-process segment traded places. In the earlier window, A19 and A20 (each running in about half of the traces, about 54 and 46 in 100) sat at roughly 36 in 100 of the trace's length, followed by A23 (about 40) and A27 (about 60), with A21 and A22 last at about 65 in 100. In the later window, A21 and A22 sat at about 38 in 100, A23 and A27 stayed near 43 and 64, and A19/A20 moved to about 67 in 100. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- Pairwise order flipped accordingly: earlier, A23 preceded A21 in about 99 in 100 traces and A27 preceded A22 in about 99 in 100; in the later window, A21 preceded A23 in about 99 in 100 and A22 preceded A27 in about 98 in 100. A19 ran before A23 in about 53 in 100 of the traces containing both earlier, while in the later window A23 ran before A19 in about 47 in 100. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL003]
- Routing at the block boundaries was redirected. A19 and A20 earlier led almost exclusively to A23 (about 99–100 in 100 of their outgoing transitions) and later almost exclusively to A28 (about 97–98 in 100); A21 and A22 earlier led mainly to A28 (about 47–52 in 100) and later mainly to A23 (about 46–50 in 100). A27 earlier fed A21/A22 (about 95 in 100) and later feeds A19/A20 (about 98 in 100); A38 earlier fed A19/A20 (about 92 in 100) and later A21/A22 (about 93 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR008]
- Direct-succession evidence matches: A21 followed by A23 within five steps in 1 trace earlier vs 199 later (mostly one or two steps apart); A21 followed by A28 in 200 traces earlier vs 1 later; A27 followed by A19 in 1 trace earlier vs 94 later; A38 followed by A21 in 1 trace earlier vs 199 later. The distance from A38 to A23 grew from two steps (about 93 in 100 traces) to three (about 90 in 100), and from A27 to A28 it shrank from three–four steps to two. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG005, LAG017, LAG019, LAG008]
- The A36–A37 repetition became less common: A36 appeared in about 24 in 100 traces earlier vs about 13 in 100 later (mean occurrences per trace 0.39 vs 0.18), and A37 returned to A36 in about 44 in 100 of its outgoing transitions earlier vs about 25 in 100 later, while continuing to A38 rose from about 56 to 72 in 100. [OCC001, DIR007, LAG015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block containing A19 and A20 and the block containing A21 and A22 exchanged their order around the unchanged A23 → A27 segment: earlier the flow ran A38 → A19 or A20 → A23 → A27 → A21 and A22 (in either order) → A28, and in the later window it runs A38 → A21 and A22 (in either order) → A23 → A27 → A19 or A20 → A28. All four moved activities shifted by roughly 0.28–0.31 of trace length, and the boundary activities rerouted their outgoing transitions exactly as this exchange implies. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR008]

The reading rests on direct relational evidence: the order flips are near-deterministic (about 98–99 in 100, with 200 traces behind each window), and participation is unchanged (A21, A22, A23 and A27 ran in every trace in both windows; A19 and A20 kept complementary shares of about half the traces each), so the same activities and paths occur and only their order and routing shares changed. The 46 flagged items also far exceed the roughly 0.67 expected by chance across the 135 tested units, so sampling variation cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [REL009, REL011, POS003, POS004, POS001, POS002]

Limitations: the outgoing transitions of A23 and A28 were not profiled, so the exact edges around the middle segment are inferred from order, position and distance evidence rather than observed directly; positions use event order, not clock time; and many items restate the same underlying exchange, so they are not independent confirmations. The evidence also cannot rule out additional changes in unprofiled parts of the process. [DIR001, DIR008, POS005, LAG001]

Other differences: the A36–A37 loop is traversed less often in the later window (A36 in about 13 in 100 traces vs about 24 earlier; A37 continuing to A38 in about 72 vs 56 in 100 of its outgoing transitions), a change in how often an existing repetition is taken that is separate from the block exchange. [OCC001, DIR007, LAG015]
